temurah-8b-9-12.note: Mar Zutra visited Rav Ashi's home, and they offered him food. They set meat before him, saying: Eat, Master, it is especially healthful, because it is a firstborn. He asked where it came from, and they said a certain priest had sold it to them. Mar Zutra asked whether they did not hold, with Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua, that this looks like a priest helping at the threshing floor; they said no, since they had bought it. He pressed them with a mishna that forbids handing a firstborn to a priest early for the same reason. They replied that there the favor is plain to see, while here they had simply bought it.
temurah-8b-9-12.why: Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua has just explained that a priest may not sell an unblemished firstborn to an Israelite, because it looks like a discount in exchange for future gifts. This incident tests that rule against a sale at fair market value.

people.name: Mar Zutra
people.about: A guest at Rav Ashi's home who questions the firstborn meat served to him.

people.name: Rav Huna son of Rabbi Yehoshua
people.about: The Sage whose rule Mar Zutra cites.

people.name: Rav Sheshet
people.about: Gives the reason behind the mishna Mar Zutra quotes.

terms.meaning: The firstborn male of a cow, sheep or goat is holy and belongs to a priest. Unblemished, it is offered on the altar; an ordinary Israelite may eat one only if it has a blemish.

terms.term: a priest who assists at the threshing floor
terms.meaning: A priest who helps a farmer at harvest so the farmer will give him his priestly gifts. The Sages forbade anything that looks like trading favors for those gifts.

temurah-15b-16-18.note: A pious man suffered from pain in his heart, and the doctors said his only cure was to drink warm milk every morning. So a goat was brought and tied to the leg of his bed, and he drank from it. When his friends came to visit and saw the goat, they exclaimed that there was an armed bandit in his house, since goats graze on neighbours' crops. They examined his conduct and found no sin in him except the goat, and on his deathbed he said the same: his only sin was keeping it against the Sages' rule.
temurah-15b-16-18.why: A teaching says the leaders of Israel after Yosef ben Yo'ezer all had some flaw. This story is raised against it: tradition identifies such a 'pious man' as a much later Sage, yet he had no flaw but the goat.

terms.meaning: Sheep and goats. The Sages forbade raising them in settled parts of the Land of Israel because they graze on other people's fields.
A teaching from the early Sages that was not included in the Mishna, the core collection of Jewish law.
